correctness.rationale: Compact positive invariant support bounds both x,y away from zero. Test generator with F′(x)=phi(x)/x and G′(y)=psi(y)/(s*y), giving E[y|x]=H(x) and E[1/x|y]=gamma/y. H(x)>0 forces x<K on support. Expanding (x-y/gamma)²/x and conditional harmonic law yields E[x|y]-y/gamma=E[(x-y/gamma)²/x|y]=s^-2 E[x*(dot y/y)²|y]≥0. Equality makes dot y=0 on invariant support and hence the unique positive equilibrium atom; distinct-degree quadratic root product ensures uniqueness. Orthogonal residuals yield both variance decompositions; nonconstant periodic orbits have nontrivial zero-mean log-coordinate speeds of both signs so cross both nullclines at least twice. Independently simplified prey and predator pointwise residual identities symbolically to zero.

originality.rationale: The source Zheng–Zhang–Li 2014 primary complete open article treats the exact positive Holling–Tanner equations, carrying-capacity invariant region, unique equilibrium and canard-cycle branches; sections 1–4 present geometric singular perturbation, not disintegration for arbitrary invariant measures. Braza 2003 original abstract concerns Hopf branches, not mean nullcline equations. Published Resultary comparison finds neighboring classic Lotka–Volterra and chemostat stationary harmonic results but not the two simultaneous conditional Holling–Tanner nullcline calibrations or their exact fiberwise dynamical activity defect. The generator and conditional Jensen/Pythagorean steps are standard methods, but their combined application to two different biological nullclines yields a precise same-model invariant-measure theorem not shown to follow from a previously published same-model stronger statement. Best-of-knowledge originality, not proof from lack of search hits.
residual_risks: A short equivalent invariant-measure generator identity may appear in older unindexed predator–prey papers; 1997 two-cycle article not read in full.
Standard conditional-expectation tools themselves are not new; claim of originality attaches only to precise same-model paired calibrations and exact dynamical defect.

value.rationale: For a natural, much-studied predator–prey oscillator, the all-invariant-measures prey conditional nullcline and predator harmonic calibration give a sharp, measurable stationary prey-excess statistic, with an exact nonnegative activity defect and rigidity to the positive equilibrium. They constrain periodic and mixed regimes independently of whether one or two cycles occur; positive support under K and mandatory crossings supply concrete model interpretation. This is a motivated structural invariant-measure classification with a precise mathematical identity, not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical recomputation; it need not classify the cycle period.
